fact: A dim red dwarf just 6 light-years away — famous for sweeping across our sky faster than any other star.
bio: Barnard's Star has the largest known proper motion of any star, crossing an apparent Moon's-width of sky roughly every 180 years — earning it the nickname 'Barnard's Runaway Star'. It is an ancient, low-mass red dwarf.
cultural: Its closeness and motion made it a long-running target in the search for nearby planets, and a staple destination in interstellar-travel fiction and early starship studies like Project Daedalus.
